I have a potentially stupid question re: onions/garlic planted in the fall

Are you meant to harvest them late fall around the first frost, or are you supposed to let them go through the winter and harvest them next spring? I feel like mine wouldn't grow fast enough to be a usable size by say late October when the real chance for a first frost hits.

I can't say for sure with onions. I know all onions like cold, but I can answer for garlic.

Plant in fall (October in these parts) and harvest in June when they die back. They love to go dormant over winter, they're just little green nubs for months. Then in the spring they explode and begin to die back.

Haven't been that successful with onions, nor have I tried.

I realized that was the best way to plant onions/garlic when my onions that I lazily left in the beds last winter (had planted them the previous spring and they didn't get very big) just blew up in the cool, wet spring.
